subject: On-prem cluster topology, node roles, and IO policy for Redwood Private deployment
messages:
From: Katherine Lowe <katherine@edgelattice.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@edgelattice.io
Date: Sat, 06 Feb 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood Private - initial cluster topology questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We sketched an initial topology and a few open questions for the on-prem install at our Denver site:

- We plan for 6 worker nodes to start, 3x GPU (A100-like) and 3x CPU-only for control-plane adjacent services. Is that an appropriate split for a P2 workload (steady inference + occasional retrain jobs)?
- Persistent volumes: we are evaluating SSD-backed LVM on top of NVMe vs Ceph OSDs. Our ops team prefers local NVMe for inference cache but wants HA for logs and artifacts. Any trade-offs you would call out?
- Eviction policy and disk pressure: defaults in k8s are brittle for bursty KV cache writes. Do you recommend an OOM or disk eviction tuning guide for the Redwood runtime?

I attached our rough diagram. Can you point us to the config knobs we should bake into the cluster plan? We can share access to the Drive folder if you need current inventory.

Best,
Katherine
Ops Lead, Edge Lattice

attachment: edge-lattice-cluster-draft-diagram.png (image/png)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Katherine Lowe <katherine@edgelattice.io>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, ops@edgelattice.io
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 09:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private - initial cluster topology questions

Katherine —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then an actionable set of recommendations below.

High level:
- Node split: 3 GPU + 3 CPU is a reasonable starting point for predictable latency. If you plan to run batching-heavy workloads, add a 4th GPU node for capacity headroom (or enable burst pools in the Dedicated model).
- Storage: use local NVMe for runtime KV/prefix cache (low latency, high IOPS). For cluster state, logging, and artifacts, use a replicated object store (S3-compatible) or Ceph with at least 3 OSDs. Mixing is fine: local NVMe for ephem cache + Ceph for durable state.
- Eviction: tune the kubelet eviction thresholds (evictionHard/evictionSoft) and mount the runtime cache to a dedicated local PV with explicit fsQuota. We also recommend a sidecar that monitors KV cache growth and triggers LRU trimming via the Redwood runtime admin API.

Actionable plan (what we can deliver in the next workshop):
1) Node role breakdown (proposal):
   - control-plane (3 masters, small CPU, high-availability)
   - inference-gpu (3 workers, 8x A100-ish GPUs total across nodes)
   - inference-cpu (2 workers, for preprocess, routing, and small-batch jobs)
   - infra (1 worker, Ceph OSDs / object gateway / logging stack)

2) Node sizing & eviction prescripts: we will produce a spreadsheet with pod density and IOPS budgets (I attached the first pass). Key knobs: kubelet.evictionHard.memory.available="200Mi", kubelet.evictionHard.nodefs.available=10%, kubelet.evictionSoft.nodefs.available=15% with grace 600s.

3) Storage pattern: local NVMe for /var/lib/redwood/cache mounted as ext4 with noatime; ensure discard is enabled if using encrypted LUKS layers. Use a replicated Ceph pool for /var/lib/redwood/artifacts and object-store backups.

4) Failure domains & affinity: separate GPU nodes across two racks, use topologySpreadConstraints for critical pods, and set podDisruptionBudgets for replicas that must remain available.

Next steps: Marcus will draft the sizing workbook and I will schedule a 60-minute design session with your ops team this week. Can you share node SKU list and expected baseline QPS for inference (tokens/sec)?

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Manager, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Quick follow-up with concrete node sizing I sketched in the spreadsheet:

- GPU nodes: 4x vCPU equivalent management cores, 512Gi RAM, 4x NVMe per node (one PV dedicated for cache at 800Gi), 8 GPUs per node is overkill for your current expected QPS — recommend 2 GPUs per node (3 nodes x 2 GPUs = 6 GPUs total) to improve single-shard latency.
- CPU worker sizing: 8vCPU/64Gi, taint these nodes as preprocess=true; tolerate-critical only.
- Ceph: prefer at least 5 OSDs for stable recovery time; dedicate infra nodes if you want isolation from inference workloads.

Eviction tuning notes I added to eviction-policy-notes.md: use node-affinity to pin cache-heavy pods to NVMe volumes and set ReadWriteMany where applicable for sidecars that aggregate logs. Also enable kubelet --eviction-pressure-transition-period=2m to react faster to transient spikes.

I uploaded the workbook (nodepool-sizing-recommendation.xlsx) with the IOPS assumptions and a projected cost delta between local NVMe + Ceph vs Ceph-only.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa and Marcus — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two quick clarifications from our infra lead: 

1) For NVMe-backed cache volumes, do you recommend LVM snapshotting for point-in-time rollback or rely on application-level checkpoints?
2) Our compliance team wants encryption-at-rest on local volumes (LUKS). Any performance guidance for LUKS + NVMe with the workloads you outlined?

We'll get you the SKU list and baseline QPS by EOD tomorrow. Please include a short runbook for recovery from a single GPU node failure (we'd like steps to bring a node back without affecting live inference).

Best,
Katherine
